The black cabinet member you're referring to is probably Robert C. Weaver, who was the first African American to serve in a presidential cabinet when he was appointed Secretary of Housing and Urban Development by President Lyndon B. Johnson in 1966. Weaver played a significant role in the civil rights movement as he worked on policies and programs aimed at promoting equality and providing better housing opportunities for low-income families and minorities. Additionally, Weaver was instrumental in the implementation of Executive Order 10925, which required government contractors to "take affirmative action to ensure that applicants are employed, and that employees are treated during employment, without regard to their race, creed, color, or national origin." Weaver's work as an advisor to the President's Committee on Government Contracts further highlights his dedication to reducing racial discrimination and increasing equal opportunities for African Americans in the housing and urban development sectors.
